title: Which way of travelling do the fewest students use?
description: The same picture of modes of travelling is read again, this time to find the way used by the fewest students. The video counts every row and finds the shortest, while Keeko doubts that walking is the least.
teaching_notes: One idea: the shortest row has the fewest students, and a guess about the real world must give way to the count. Watch for children who choose a row by what seems likely instead of counting.

source: Pictograph: modes of travelling, which is used by the least number of students
video_script.why: The child reads the same picture to find the smallest count, by counting and not by guessing.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own picture of modes of travelling
video_script.anchor: the picture of five modes of travelling with a row of smileys for each
video_script.wrong_answer: walking is used by the least number of students
video_script.wrong_move: guesses that walking is the least because it needs no vehicle, without comparing the rows
video_script.payoff_line: The cycle is used by the least number of students, three of them.
maths_rules: Private car 4, public bus 5, school bus 11, cycle 3, walking 7.
The shortest row, 3 smileys, is the cycle.
video_script.design: Five rows of smileys under a key, each row labelled with its mode of travel.

beats.on_screen: title card with five rows of smileys, labelled private car, public bus, school bus, cycle and walking

marks.scene: the title card arrives with the five rows
marks.rows: the five rows light up one after another
marks.ask: a question mark lights up beside the rows

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a picture from your book about how students travel to school.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>Each row shows one way of travelling, and each row has smileys.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which way of travelling is used by the fewest students?

beats.on_screen: the five rows and the question mark stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: two rows of smileys, one short and one long, with the key one smiley equals one student beside them

marks.short: the short row is labelled fewer students
marks.long: the long row is labelled more students

narration: <bookmark mark='short'/>A row with fewer smileys stands for fewer students.
<bookmark mark='long'/>A row with more smileys stands for more students.

beats.on_screen: Given: key 1 smiley = 1 student; rows: private car, public bus, school bus, cycle, walking

marks.given: the key and the five labelled rows are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, five rows: private car, public bus, school bus, cycle and walking.

beats.on_screen: To find: the mode of travel used by the least number of students

marks.find: the line to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the way of travelling used by the fewest students.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: read the key: 1 smiley = 1 student, so each smiley counts as 1

marks.key: the key at the top of the picture is circled

narration: One smiley is one student, so each smiley counts as one.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: count the smileys: private car 4, public bus 5, school bus 11, cycle 3, walking 7

marks.first: the smileys of the first three rows are counted and the numbers are written
marks.last: the smileys of the last two rows are counted and the numbers are written

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, count the smileys in each row. Private car has four, public bus has five, and school bus has eleven.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Cycle has three, and walking has seven.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: compare the counts: 3 is smaller than 4, 5, 7 and 11

marks.compare: the shortest row is circled and the other counts are set beside it

narration: Three is smaller than four, five, seven and eleven.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The cycle is used by the least number of students, three of them.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: the walking row with a cross, and the cycle row laid beside it, clearly shorter, with a tick

marks.fix: the cycle row is laid beside the walking row and is clearly shorter
marks.count: the smileys of the two rows are counted aloud, three and seven

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks walking is used by the least number of students, because walking needs no vehicle.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But that is only a guess, and the picture must decide.
<bookmark mark='count'/>The walking row has seven smileys, and the cycle row has only three.
